title: The ending of the story
body: Two nights before the Derby, Paul's mother hurries home from a party, seized by anxiety about her son. In the dark bedroom she finds him riding his rocking-horse in a frenzy. He screams the name 'Malabar' and falls to the floor unconscious, with brain-fever. When the mother asks what Malabar means, Uncle Oscar tells her it is one of the horses running in the Derby, and he himself puts a thousand pounds on Malabar at fourteen to one. On the third day of the illness, Bassett comes to the bedside and whispers that Malabar has won and that Paul now has over eighty thousand pounds. Paul cries out that he is lucky and that, if he rides his horse till he is sure, he knows the winner. He dies that night. Uncle Oscar says to his sister that she is eighty-odd thousand to the good and a poor devil of a son to the bad, and that the boy is best gone out of a life where he rides his rocking-horse to find a winner.
